title: Network security groups and application security groups

videos.script: A network security group is a list of rules. Each one allows or denies traffic. {{list}} The list is read from the top, by priority, and the first rule that matches decides. Nothing below it is read. {{first}} Every list starts with six rules you did not write. Together they say three things. {{defaults}} Inside the network, everything may talk to everything. From outside, nothing comes in. And everything may go out. {{wide}} Two of those three are too generous for a shop that keeps customers' orders. {{narrow}} So you write rules about roles instead of addresses. A tag names a set of Microsoft's addresses. An application security group names a set of your machines. {{groups}} Then you walk packets through the rules, one at a time, with a small program of the course's own. {{walk}} One of them is a health probe that your own rule shuts out. Finding it in a model is cheaper than finding it in production. {{end}}
